newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside to fund expansion internally.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside to fund expansion internally.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Thursday it would use cash flow and existing debt facilities to fund its share of the A$6.0 billion proposed expansion of the North-West Shelf gas project offshore Western Australia.
"We would be funding our share through internal cash flow and existing loan facilities we have in place," Woodside's corporate affairs manager Geoff Wedgwood told Reuters.

Woodside, which is 40 percent owned by Royal Dutch/Shell Group, is an equal 16.66 percent shareholder in the project. Royal Dutch/Shell is also a partner in the giant liquefied natural gas (LNG) project.

Wedgwood said Woodside had refinanced its debt facilities recently. On October 2, Woodside completed the refinancing of its corporate debt facilities, cancelling US$1.45 billion in debt and drawing down US$1.2 billion under a new facility.
The new facility is in two tranches of US$950 million for five years and US$250 million for seven years.
The other project partners are BHP Petroleum (North West Shelf) Pty Ltd, BP Developments Australia Ltd, Chevron Asiatic Ltd and Japan Australia LNG (MIMI) Pty Ltd.
Wedgwood said work on the development of the proposed project expansion would not start until late 1998, pending agreement with the major buyers of the project's LNG customers in Japan.
The expansion would add about seven million tonnes per annum making an annual sales capacity of about 14.5 million by the year 2003, Wedgwood said.

"The next thing that is likely to be a letter of intent in late 1997 for the development of this expansion proposal," Wedgwood said. He said between now and then there are lots of talks on technical issues surrounding the expansion proposal.
"Following that would be a purchase agreement between the North West shelf partners and the Japanese buyers, which would be around late 1998," Wedgwood said.
Wedgwood said the Shelf partners had not been in any formal talks with partners in the nearby Gorgon gas project, which has the capacity to produce six million LNG tonnes per annum.

"The North West shelf partners have their own plans for expansion, but if the Gorgon partners have a good proposal that we can work together then we will certainly have a look at it," Wedgwood said. "But to date we have not seen a plan that fits within our plans."
Shell owns two-sevenths of the Gorgon field. The other partners are Chevron, Texaco Inc and Mobil Corp's unit Ampolex Ltd.
Wedgwood said there was also considerable potential for domestic gas expansion in the North West Shelf due to increased industrial use in Western Australia.

"There are also plans for a significant domestic gas expansion due to increased demand from industrial users of gas," Wedgwood said. Some of Australia's largest miners have targetted North West Shelf gas as a power source for project expansions.
At 1.30 p.m. (0330 GMT), Woodside shares were one cent up at A$8.76 after earlier hitting a high of A$8.80.
